what: Layout of The Librarian index Sheet. Fetched at setup by docs-librarian-getting-started so every install builds the same Sheet. Replaces index-sheet-layout.json (v1): the date column now covers renewals, endings, expiries and paid-up-to dates, Days left is a formula, and the Renewals tab records when a date was flagged.
rules: Written for a person to read first.
Row 1 is the headers and stays frozen.
A cell the document does not fill stays blank. Nothing else means 'not in the document': no dashes, no 'Not recorded', no guesses.
No ID codes, no row numbers, no backup tabs.
The Days left formula counts from the spreadsheet's own timezone: ask the owner to set File > Settings > Time zone to theirs, as the bot cannot set it.
renews_or_ends: Use the date the document says the thing renews, ends or expires.
For something paid up to a date, use the last day paid for.
If one document carries several such dates, add one Renewals row per date, and keep the earliest date still in the future on the Documents row.
A date that has already passed stays on Documents and is not added to the Renewals tab.
A date the document only estimates stays blank.

tabs.name: Documents
tabs.note: One row per document in your library.

columns.what: Card policy, insurance, contract, tenancy, utility, subscription, other

The message the document came in; the copy in Drive or another service; or the path on the owner's computer, then the message link

tabs.name: Renewals
tabs.note: What is coming up, soonest first. Future dates only, one row per date.

columns.what: A formula, filled down the column, so it stays right between runs
The date this row was flagged. Blank until it is. Cleared if the date itself changes
